tips.comment: Analogical makes his handicap debut after three runs in novices and now steps up in trip. He’s on a low mark and could take a decent step forward if he stays the distance.

Nicely bred 3yo filly. Three career runs. She was a runner-up two weeks ago in a maiden race, bumping into a smart looking winner. No answer in the final 2f but she did match the winner for the first mile and still saw the race out, in that strongly run contest. She should get a more suitable pace in this low grade handicap and she could prove to be better than her opening mark of 60.

Gungnir returns as a gelding and could progress from what he showed as a juvenile. He finished 3rd on his last start and now runs off a workable mark. David Allan rides for Tim Easterby, a trainer who knows how to win here. He looks primed to surprise, and at 14/1, there’s definite value. ???'?
This is the trainer's only entry he's got out today, and they have got the regular jockey back on board. A good value each way bet.
Yet to win a race, but this lightly used filly took a step in the right direction on 2/7 at Wolverhampton 16 days ago. That sort of form would put her in the mix in this race today.

Lightly raced and now dropping to a Class 6 handicap, Arie Gordye could easily improve. He has a decent RPR of 67, and trainer Adrian Nicholls often finds success with this type of runner. With Harrison Shaw booked, he's nicely weighted and drawn. At 12/1, he's a solid each-way play in a very open race. ??'???'?
Has been in good form over hurdles and on the flat and won at Brighton over 1m2f with a little bit in hand. Gone up in the handicap but this race lacks any depth.
This filly remains unexposed on turf for Michael Baal, who is in great form at the moment. This can be the answer to this puzzle here, with a strong performance likely.

Didn't perform to usual form on A/W recently after proving to be somewhat of a serial placer prior. Off the back of a decent 4th back on grass last time out, this looks like a good opportunity to get the long-awaited win.

Jenson Benson is on the same last mark here. He is a consistent type, but has had no win in the last 21 starts. However, at Brighton, he got an improving 4th and was not beaten by far. He is often thereabouts in his races, and it is possible he could upset today.
Looks sure to go close after second last time, running on very well. A step up in trip must eke out a bit more. Solid chance for me here.
Ivane moved to the new yard of James Owen earlier this year and finished top 3 in all 4 races for the new yard including a win in Southwell. I also expect a win for Ivane today.

Four starts over hurdles for the 4yo, one win, three decent runs in defeat. Not disgraced in a Grade 3 handicap last time out, when racing from 9lb out of the handicap. She likes the better ground and is now running in a class 5 handicap against older runners, but she does receive an 8lb age allowance. Top yard/jockey, more to come from this one.
Not much form here, but Basman Palace, a progeny of Silvano, catches the eye and has found his form at the right time. He will contest the finish and probably win.

The model I run suggests Pub Crawl can get over the line first here. Pub Crawl has an RPR towards the top of the order but has an official ranking that allows him to carry lighter weight. Last run 32 days ago, so has race fitness and has some form coming into this, with a prior 2nd and 4th at Sedgefield.

Little Pi was only 3.5 L behind Ivane last time out and is 3lb better off in this today. He was not strongly pushed out last time in the last 100 yards, and with the ground not as soft, he has a chance to reverse those placings today. In doing so, he should find himself in the first three at least.
Even though he remains a maiden over hurdles, 17 attempts, he has been running fairly well, grabbing 4 places from his last 8 starts. New trainers, maybe they can find that little bit extra required.
Harry Skelton takes over the reins for the first time, and it would be no surprise to see this horse do better than previous runs for the yard, now having had some time to find her feet again.

Good stable. This one comes with massive risks, has run out and has also refused to run. Last time out at Stratford, it was reluctant to start before racing in the rear. Made good headway from 2 out and led at the last, going clear on the run-in to easily beat Kankin. The ability is there and can follow up if starting on terms.
The Wire Flyer caught the eye last time, winning with ease and with plenty in hand over 4000m. Elizabeth Gayle retains the ride and she can repeat if maintaining her last form.
Jackpot Cash is an improver over both hurdles and fences. His current chase mark of 106 could still underestimate his ability, and he looks to have this match race in the bag.

The model I run suggests Zero Tolerance can win this race. Zero Tolerance has the middle-ranked RPR of the 3 runners but goes out carrying the lowest weight thanks to having a lower official ranking. It has the joint highest top speed on the card for this race and last ran 59 days ago. Jackpot Cash, the current market leader, last raced only 7 days ago, and you wonder whether the turnaround is too quick.

Five-time winner Gavin bounced back to form with a win at Ffos Las last week. He won easily there by 9.5 lengths. He has a 7lb penalty, but with Sean Bowen booked to ride, he looks the most likely winner here.

The model I run suggests each way on Jet Patrol is the value bet here. There are 3 places up for grabs on some of the bookies, such as B365. Lewis Dobb on board is claiming a hefty 7 lbs, which takes the total weight carried for Jet Patrol down to 10-5. This is a significant difference to the market leader of over 1 stone over this 2m round trip. With 3 runners placing in a 7 runner race, this has to be the value bet at 15s.

Mr Sundancer has been on my radar for a while and whilst we have a hot fave in this race we may be able to come in EW as he won at Downpatrick last year, but has been a little underwhelming since switching yards. His mark is falling (down to 98 today) and this better ground may suit.

The addition of the tongue tie looks significant given the consistency she has shown in previous starts. This looks like a good opportunity to get on the scoreboard. She looks to be a very big player.
Solent Gateway moved to the new yard of McCain jr and also had wind surgery. He finished top 3 in the last 3 races and I expect a win for Solent Gateway today.

The model I run suggests Celestial Reign can cause an upset here. Steps out with a middle-ranking RPR but goes out carrying the lowest weight of the 7 runners over this 2m 3f trip. Unlucky to be brought down in March and ran a decent 4th in April at this course. Looking to build on that here over a similar distance.
This race doesn't look the strongest, so this lightly raced gelding could go well, especially if there is money for him before the off.
This horse looks like it could be his turn again after not being able to quite get a win in the UK yet, but had 3 in France. Likely to be well ridden by Sean Bowen and can win this one.

CONQUER THE BREEZE has been placed in a hurdle race and a chase from eleven NH starts. Second in a chase over 2m at Sedgefield on his latest outing last month. Course, distance, and going should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to go one better and win this race.

Clean Getaway showed below-par performance at Carlisle last time, but that's a tougher track. He goes well on similar going, proven at this course, loves the tight Sedgefield layout. Thriving at this track and could come on for reappearance.

There could be others but both Bet365 and Betfred are currently betting to three places each way in this six runner field, and both go 6/1 bog about Fearless Action. Eased a couple of pounds since his last run and with Danny McMenamin back on board for the first time since the partnership was successful over today's course and distance in March, I think there's plenty of value to be had.

The model I run suggests each way on Jackhammer is the play here. Jackhammer is not fancied at all in the early market. The result of the model has largely been driven by Jackhammer having the highest RPR of the field and at 11 YO has plenty of experience. Ranked bottom in the official rankings, and goes out carrying the very bottom in terms of weights. Charlie Maggs on board claims a further 5 lbs on top of that, which brings the total weight difference to the top of the market to 2 stone 2 lbs.

BELLE NA BANN has won four hurdle races from 2m to 2m 2f. Pulled up in a hurdle race over 2m at Perth on her latest outing last month. Over fences today, course distance and going should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to win this race.

Drops in grade after C&D win earlier in April and last time out dominant display in a Class 4 event. Ran on with plenty to spare and raised only 6 lb for this performance. Back in C5 company over a track he clearly likes - has been a dominant winner since wind surgery and cheekpieces went on - today's claimer takes off 7 lb.
Laravie had a strong race in February on this course with a second place in a strong field. I give Laravie a good chance to grab the win in the race today.

The model I run suggests Lillistar can win what looks like a fairly open race. Lillistar has the second highest RPR ranking of the 7 runners but goes out carrying the significantly lower of the weights over this 2m 3f trip. Other runners have claiming jockeys on board, which muddies the water somewhat, but Lillistar still carries the lowest amount when lining up, taking the total weight differential into consideration.

Super unlucky to bump into Mermaids Cave at the beginning of her winning run (now 25lb higher) at Fontwell and the betting seemed to know that the eight-year-old was subsequently finished for the season.
The Jamie Snowden-trained inmate makes her return after a 334-day absence, but I doubt she will be lacking for fitness on this long journey north.
Unbelievable chance if reproducing her penultimate second.

This looks like a very poor bumper, and I'll be surprised if Dartmouth Castle doesn't come out on top. He ran pretty well on debut at Doncaster, where the opposition came from stables that generally do well in this sphere. He must give weight all around, apart from Scairp Dubh. However, he can win with a bit to spare.

The 6yo has 7 career wins. Not beaten far two starts back, something amiss last time out on the AW but he’s been given a seven week break to freshen up. Two huge turf runs this time last year, a close 4th of 26 followed by a close 2nd of 20. The majority of runners in that second race were rated 78-85. He now has a 5lb lower mark, like the fast ground, facing just one rival rated above 73 and the strong jockey booking is a positive move… plenty of ticks in the right boxes.

Good form from the three main players in this novice stakes. The selection is the only runner with turf form and the benefit of a recent run. Good yard/jockey. Runner-up in her last start but well clear of the 3rd and 4th who both had good ratings going into that maiden race. She also receives a nice pull at the weights in this maiden race.

Lightly raced 4yo. Solid form last year in quality handicap races, over this 6f trip and on fast ground. A big run at the start of the month, losing by a hd in a 13 runner £52K handicap. He was coming off a 7 month break that day and you would hope he can take a step forward. Should be a big player in this handicap with Ryan Moore now taking over in the saddle.

Holkham Bay was quite unlucky at Goodwood as he was stuck behind horses which were dropping back. He got in the clear too late and was therefore given an easy ride. He loves York and will appreciate the rain. He's not obviously well handicapped, but could still be a couple of pounds too low.

Commanche Falls is slowly but surely getting back to a more reasonable mark. His run at Leicester wasn't as bad as he was drawn worst of all, and only the winner was able to get competitive from a low draw. He likes it here, and the rain can only help.

Comes into the race on the back of two good wins over this 6f trip on the AW, the last one in a fast time at Newcastle last month. Still only a 4-year-old, and the yard has won the last two runnings of this event.

This horse has reappeared in good order, going close on two occasions. He’s up in class here. He’ll benefit from a lesser weight carry, albeit in stronger company. But in a race that offers no out-and-out potential superstar, he could be getting himself involved in the shake-up from a high draw. A pricey purchase as a yearling, he’s related to some smart sorts, and producing his best speed figure last time, he could just be in good enough form to take to this step up in class.

First Folio has a chance of making the frame (5). His best run last year was at Hamilton when finishing 3rd of 9 off a BHA 87. If he can return to that level of form off the same mark from stall 2, he looks value at around 20/1. Jockey choice is a plus with Joe Fanning off a low weight. Could make all the running.
Looks the one on form with the absence of stablemate Kalpana. This trip and ground are perfect. I'm on at 4/1.
Looks sure to run a big race. He looks the EW steal, but I just feel See The Fire is a bit better. She is regally bred.

Talking Horse since Acomb win here from subsequent Guineas winner Ruling Court. May not be fully fit, but if he's the horse they think he is, you'd imagine he'd be winning here. Don't mind taking a 50/50 here.

Lingfield novice winner who reappeared with a mighty effort to land the listed Blue Riband Trial at Epsom at 40/1. That's amongst the best form on offer here so would be no surprise to see this son of Sea The Stars run very well at a price.

Likely the class act here, and they fancy him for a Group horse later in the season. Not an ideal draw to contend with, but they're likely to go very fast here, and a pace collapse would set up nicely for this one, barring traffic problems. Quite impressive win first time out last time and had much more in hand than the 0.75L would suggest.

Seems to have been forgotten about her slightly, but was mixing it with the best back in '23 with multiple Group placings. Is clearly quite inconsistent; however, ran well at Goodwood off 94, won next time out off 94. End of the season run 2.5L behind Shagraan off 97 wasn't a bad run at all with how the form has worked out. Good seasonal debut, then ran no sort of race next time. Drawn low, however, and claims 5lbs again.

Lightly raced 3yo filly. Two runs this year. Excuses last time out when not firing on her AW debut. Only beaten 2L on her return during March, in a very strong looking Listed contest against older runners. She wasn’t beaten far at this track last summer, on fast ground, in a Group 2 contest. She now drops into a class 3 handicap, her mark of 94 looks very handy and she’s now helped by a capable apprentice who is taking a useful 7lb off her back.

The selection is making his debut in this average looking 6 runner novice stakes. The trainer has good career stats with his 2yo runners, sending out plenty of quality youngsters in recent years. You would expect he’d be using one of his better types with a first prize of £20K in this contest.

Great Bedwyn is a horse who has outrun his odds both times he has run at York, which is a track that doesn't suit a lot of horses. He also seems to go well first time out and his trainer Richard Hannon is operating at a very good strike rate considering the number of runners he has.

The 4yo progressed nicely last year, winning 2 of his last 3 runs in 2024. He was a good 3rd of 13 on his return last month after a 7 month break - high RPR rating posted - and can take another step forward. He was a nice 4L winner on fast ground last year.

Ottoman is a lot more interesting than the form book on paper is suggesting returned to action on the 7th of April 2025 after a 161 day break having exchanged hands and joined a new stable in the process of that break now after 2 runs for his new yard he arrives here in a much fitter state and is better adjusted back home at his new yard steps up in trip going over 1 mile 2 furlongs for the first time that being a good move by his connections as this new trip can unlock a whole new level of improvement currently operating on a very dangerous mark of 54 O Greenall & J Guerriero's new recruit looks poised to trouble the judge on this outing jockey Aiden Brookes takes off a handy 3lb which only enhances his good looking claims here in what is a suitable assignment for this individual likely to be a whole different proposition this time out especially over this new trip gelded son of Acclamation & Kaftan ( Dam's sire Dansili ) must be taken very seriously of this sort of mark and shouldn't be by any means underestimated

Ex-French runner Iowa City comes over with some fair form, having never finished out of the first three, including a listed race. But distance winner and very well-bred Faiyum looked very impressive when winning a maiden in her only run. She had to come from behind a wall of horses and, despite running green, looked to win with something in hand. That form looks very strong as three of those beaten horses have since won.
Gun Carriage can get off the mark here unless there is something lurking that we don't know about. Would that surprise you? No, really! It's horse racing.

Standard Deviation is a 3-year-old gelding trained by P Twomey. He makes his second start, having finished fourth on debut at Gowran and clearly needed the experience. Standard Deviation has a lovely pedigree, being out of an unraced dam out of Galileo, who was related to four individual winners, two of which posted career-high RPR of 102-111. Standard Deviation will probably want a longer trip in time but should be staying on strongly at the end of today's mile for a yard that has an amazing record with horses running who have never won or are making their debut. P Twomey has a 31.2% win strike rate, 90/288 wins since 2012, showing a healthy LSP of £96.53 with such horses since 2012, and Standard Deviation should show up well under Billy Lee.

Joseph Patrick O'Brien has fielded 2 colts at once for this race. Dancingondiamonds is one of them. A good pedigree, a high price of 220,000 euros, excellent stats from the stable, and jockey Dylan Browne McMonagle in the last 2 weeks are the factors that make this bet quite logical.

At 25/1, this is a bit of a long shot for the first run. However, Valorous Power is from a Frankel colt with a very strong pedigree. The yard also stables Dancingondiamonds, who seems to be their first shout. However, Valorous Power could offer better value at bigger odds, so going EW.

Stepped up to 1m6f for the first run of the season 5 weeks ago at Gowran. Second that day and was running on which means the 1m6f today will not be a problem. He was running over shorter distances last season in Group races and got within 7l of Economics in the Dante this time last year. Comic Book is the only danger but needs the ground to be soft.

Has been well beaten on her first two starts since joining this yard last month following a break of almost five months. Placed in two of her three starts last year over similar trips to today. Julian Pietropaolo's 7lb claim should help. Good EW bet.

Royal Entry is a 4-year-old filly making her stable debut for P Twomey in a first-time visor. She has 0-6 wins but has run with credit, being rated 85. She is a full sister to three winners, notably Smash Williams RPR 112. So, Royal Entry should be more than capable of winning a maiden at Killarney and should make it a good day for trainer P Twomey, who is 59/161 wins with horses who have run but never won, boasting a 36.6% win strike rate since 2012 and Royal Entry is my short priced banker of the day.

Robbies Rock has won on the flat and over hurdles, with his last start in that sphere an excellent second in the Fred Winter at Cheltenham. He was 4th of 15 at Tipperary when returned to the flat at Tipperary last month. He looks a good each way bet with 4 places on offer off a 1lb lower mark.

Zanahiyr looks exceptionally well handicapped on the Flat off a mark of 77 (jockey Declan McDonogh carries 9 stone 1 pound). Rated at a peak of 159 in the past over hurdles, trailed Honeysuckle, Constitution Hill and State Man in Grade 1 hurdle competition. Has a blend of speed and stamina (by Nathaniel out of a Marju dam which makes some sense). This 2 miles 1 furlong trip looks ideal. Best backed horse in the race, looks a value play at win odds of 11-2.

Dual purpose horse ran well in the Martin Pipe over hurdles, meeting trouble in running and again found trouble on the flat last time. That was over 14f, and he is certain to appreciate this longer trip. I expect money to be piling on this one, especially with him acting on any ground.

Galway winner at today's trip back in July last year and most recently winner of a Cross Country race twelve days ago, confirming his current well-being. Could take all the beating now returned to the level.
With Seamus Heffernan taking the ride for the Queally yard, it might be worth an interest. Made a nice return to racing last time out and looks likely to build on that run.

Ran to form, beaten 7L in a handicap over 12f at Tipperary last time. Not yet proven at this trip, but providing stamina holds up, was a good fourth, only three and a half lengths over 1m6f at Navan. NB
Is actually on a hat-trick, although very spread out. Should be fit after a recent run over jumps, and although it looks like I have missed the bigger price, 14-1 still looks ok.

Jabbar is a 6-year-old gelding trained by Gerard O'Leary. He is a very talented dual-purpose horse, winning 7 out of 22 races. His only win over hurdles was when he beat a 1/9 favorite, The Enabler, and is now rated 133, an incredibly high rating for one start. He's won six times on the flat and has risen some 35 lbs from an opening 65 to 90. He is 2 for 2 wins at Killarney and handles today's ground well. He won this time last year on the 13th of May. Today, he has the capable assistance of jockey Keithen Kennedy, who has been riding with confidence of late, picking up three winners. His 5 lb apprentice claim could prove invaluable.
Won a non-official race last but still a serious horse on flat despite spending the last chunk of race time doing hurdles. Dual-purpose winner and on a competitive mark.
This gelding has a long absence to overcome, but with the yard being in form, I'm hoping that he can go well over hurdles, having been quite useful on the flat.

Interesting debut for this stable today. Has what appears to be good handicap form in Germany, including a win in a race that produces a number of subsequent winners, so clearly has ability. Has been racing over shorter distances, so it's interesting that connections step up to 2 miles for this race. Lightly raced 5yo horse, so open to plenty of improvement and is in the right hands with this trainer. Trainer and jockey enjoy good results partnering up, and this is the jockey's only booked ride here today. This horse could be thrown in at the weights if notable improvement has taken place since last seen on a racecourse.

A 3-time winner on the flat and 3 times over jumps, who was not beaten far when finishing 8th in last season's Cesarewitch on penultimate start. Has run well first time out in the past, including a win back in April 2022, who could go well here at a big price.

Kate Knows Best was 6/5 favourite last time out but finished tamely. She had decent form prior to that, so with a drop back to 2m, this should suit her. She can go very well from fresh and will, if fully tuned up and ready for this run, she could strike home first. Every chance if returning sound today.

ENCOSTA could be more than just a project for handicap hurdles. She heralds from a high-profile dual-purpose yard and hseh has a flat rating which makes her a mare of enough ability to have a say in this level on maiden hurdle. Value shout.

Harry The Rogue was a respectable sixth last time at Gowran Park after winning at Naas. He could bounce back to winning ways here tonight. With luck in running, he could certainly be involved in the finish.

Saxon Kingdom is still a maiden after 22 starts, but recent runs suggest his turn is near. He was 6th of 20, beaten just 2.5 lengths at Leopardstown in March before finishing runner-up at Dundalk a week later. He was only 8th at Curragh last week, but that was over 7 furlongs. Back at 8 furlongs off a 5 lbs lower mark, he looks a good each way bet with 4 places on offer.
The maiden tag still bugs me for Deuteronomy from the Burns combo, but it's going better than it looks and gets a chance off this low rating and a good draw here.

Mogwli won for me the other day and had apprentice jockey Megan Telford-Kelly, who takes off ten pounds. She was not hard on the horse when winning at Gowran Park. Gone up seven pounds but could be carrying this off with distinction.
This is the trainer's only entry he's got out today, and they have got the same jockey on board. A good value each-way bet for the 4 places available.

A more exposed bunch you won’t find. It might pay to side with one of the least exposed ones in Mark Fahy’s ARTHUR ROSE. This lightly raced 4 y/o filly has had 2 spins on the turf this year, both on soft ground, and hasn’t shown a whole pile. Back down in trip today and encountering faster ground, this might be a good opportunity for her to show an improvement in form. There isn’t much of a bias here, but you wouldn’t want to be drawn too high, so trap 2 offers another bit of mild encouragement. Fahy’s stable is purring along nicely, and at 16/1 I’ll chuck a penny in the well.

RELEVANT RANGE has run well at this venue previously and and is third-up for this spell with potential to peak. His latest effort is probably best ignored on unsuitable testing ground and ace apprentice Darragh O'Sullivan has winning form on this experienced type.

Eammon O'Connell’s 7-year-old gelding SAY YOU'RE SORRY can be forgiven for the hoof rust 60 days ago at Dundalk (11f), and should/could strip fitter here after a 211-day break. This son of OCOVANGO has yet to shed his maiden tag, but it looked like the penny had started to drop in his last two runs - both on the all-weather - over today’s trip, finishing 4th twice (beaten 2 and 1¼ lengths) off a mark of 54.
He arrives here at Killarney, where the left-handed, flat, and sharp characteristics of the track could potentially spark improvement from this lightly raced charge (and by 'lightly raced' I’m, of course, referencing his turf record with only three starts to date). As a fellow tipster (and good friend) has already noted, this field is very exposed, and I’d also prefer to side with a higher-priced, less exposed contender.
With 5lbs less to carry, a left-handed sharp track, and a pipe-opener now in the tank, I’m happy to take my chance. And who knows? If the equine gods are in a forgiving mood, they may just smile down on this one and maybe even on me.
Very lightly raced for a 5-year-old and not much to write home about based on recent form, but has shown some ability before entering handicaps. Mark reduced by three pounds and gamble taken on her.
Banker bet of the day for your multiple bets. Has already won a point. The most experienced of this field, and the drop in distance from previous start looks ideal.

Paymelater is a 6-year-old gelding trained by the little-known S Michael Millar and is owned and ridden by Mr. N Gault, so the jockey has a vested interest. There's nothing much to shout about regarding the pedigree line, but he did shape well last time out when finishing 3/15 at Tramore, RPR 91, behind More Coko, RPR 100, beaten 7.75 lengths, taking that placing in the closing stages so today's longer trip should help. More Coko has won twice since and is rated 127. The 5/15 Reiki Revolution won next time out at 40-1, so the form looks solid, and Paymelater should go close today.

Up against a hot favorite today, so may hit the EW places. Shudawudacuddagh was in 6th behind Cosmos D’ainay, and to be fair, was not that far off. A chance is taken today to chase the favorite home or even reverse the form.

2 podium finishes from 7 previous hurdles outings for Maroto and can be sided with here in a serious drop in terms of field quality. Has had a couple of leg stretcher outings in Dec and Jan and should be all the better for them here.
The tentative selection in this one has to show that the ground suits. But if it does, then it looks to have the form to make the frame here.
Sole hurdle win came on good ground at Sligo, so fair to assume that The Truant will run well given decent recent flat form.
The yard's form at the course is what attracts me to this one as they do very well here. This gelding has already won over the course and distance off a one-pound lower mark.

Highland Earl is a 5-year-old gelding trained by Liam P. Cusack. He has yet to trouble the judge in five starts hurdling and has dropped to a career-low handicap mark of 85. Liam P. Cusack has picked up 5 winners from his last 14 runners at Sligo, so he clearly targets this meeting. Highland Earl's mark of 85 should be workable given he's a fifth foal and half-brother to two winning hurdlers who posted career-high RPR of 122-124. He could play a big part today under Richard Deegan.
Lightly raced and unexposed, was travelling well in front when falling two out at Clonmel last time. Off same mark, and commands consideration.

APPLEJACK POET second run back is a speculative selection in a modest enough looking handicap hurdle. Not highly-tried still possibly with more to offer and jockey Tom Harney offers excellent value for the 7lb he is still allowed to claim. Fully effective on ground this quick he could be worth a market check.
On a long losing streak but gained her only win to date at this track, she runs off a career low mark, and she has run well under today's rider in the past.
With the stable in very good form, it might be worth a small interest on this seven-year-old who has become very well handicapped. The extra furlong here should be a plus.
